⑧ 专利公报（官方专利公报）
我们正在征求知识产权专业人士（尤其是专利专家）的意见！
2022年1月12日及之后发布的公报。

日本特许厅（JPO）明确指出，“专利公报是指从公报发布网站以XML格式提供的公报。”

“XML格式”是指类似以下文档首页所示的格式：

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C

此外，日本特许厅在2022年1月11日之前发布的PDF格式公报已被废止。

此前，这些已被废止的PDF格式公报被视为“官方公报”。

这是因为当时只有日本特许厅发布的公报才是官方公报。

自2022年1月12日起，包括INPIT在内的许多私营企业开始分发使用各自方法制作的“专有PDF出版物”。

INPIT还指出，“出版物采用XML格式，因此没有版式或页数限制”，并且“因此不存在标准出版物版式/页数的概念”。

此外，他们还声称“出版物采用XML格式，将其转换为PDF格式没有任何限制”。

另外，INPIT表示，“无意将J-PlatPat提供的PDF指定为‘标准’，并且我们认为私营企业提供的PDF也会被分发”。

因此，“真正的专利出版物”仅指日本特许厅出版物网站提供的“XML格式”，而INPIT和各私营企业制作的“专有PDF出版物”不能被视为“法律认可的出版物”。

如上所述，从 J-PlatPat 下载的“专有PDF 出版物”与从私营公司（例如日立系统公司的 SRPARTNER）获得的“专有PDF 出版物”各不相同，均不能被视为“正版出版物”。

从 INPIT 的 J-PlatPat 下载的“PDF 出版物”仅为“专有 PDF 出版物”，不能被视为“正版出版物”。

此外，私营公司制作的“专有 PDF 出版物”也不能被视为“正版出版物”。

关于“专有 PDF 出版物”的发布，INPIT 的 J-PlatPat 历史上曾发生过一件奇怪的事件。

不知何故，2022 年 1 月 12 日至 1 月 24 日这 13 天内从 J-PlatPat 下载的“专有 PDF 出版物”出现了异常。

https://t.co/iIBNCtOcDR

具体来说，首页右下角显示的“代表性图纸”以及第3页的图纸部分缺失。

此外，2022年1月20日发布的“JP 2022-014916”专有PDF版本也存在代表性图纸和其他图纸缺失的情况。

https://t.co/fiIqp9T5N8

另一方面，由私营公司日立系统（Hitachi Systems）从SRPARTNER下载的“JP 2022-014916”专有PDF版本则没有缺失任何部分。

https://t.co/lCT5dRre7A

从 J-PlatPat 下载的“专有PDF 出版物”的怪异之处似乎一直持续到同年 1 月 24 日。

https://t.co/PrVwFrEG9m

代表性图纸（图3）第 (2) 部分存在遗漏。

鉴于这令人遗憾的 13 天经历，我对从J-PlatPat 下载的、由 INPIT 提供的“专有PDF 出版物”的可靠性深表怀疑。

（日本語原文）

くた・れAI 。AI依存症になるな ! AIを恋人にするな ！　AIを使うな、自分で考えて文章を書け ! !

⑧法令上の公報（真正な特許公報）
知財関係者（特に、特許担当者）のコメントを求む !!

2022年１月１２日以降の公報。

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」、と明言しています。

そして、「ＸＭＬ形式」とは、以下の資料のフロントページにあるようなものです。

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C

また、2022年１月１１日以前に特許庁より発行されていたPDF公報は廃止されました。

従来は、この廃止されたPDF公報が「真正な公報」とみなされてきたと思います。

何となれば、特許庁が発行するものが唯一のものでしたので。

2022年１月１２日以降は、INPITをはじめ、多くの民間のベンダーが独自の手法により作成したものが、「独自PDF公報」として流通しています。

そして、INPITは、「公報はＸＭＬですので、レイアウトもページも存在しません。」、「したがって、公報標準レイアウト/ページの概念はございません。」ともいっています。

更に、「公報はＸＭＬであり、ＰＤＦ化するに当たっての制限はありません。」と断言しています。

加えて、INPITは「J-PlatPatから提供されるPDFを「標準」とする意図はなく、民間事業者が提供するPDFも流通すると考えております。」、と回答しています。

従って、「真正な特許公報」とは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから提供される「XML形式」のみのもので、INPITや各民間業者の作成した「独自PDF公報」は「法令上の公報」とはいえないことになります。

以上の如く、J-PlatPatからダウンロードして得られる「独自PDF公報」や、民間業者、たとえば日立システムズのSRPARTNERより得られる「独自PDF公報」などは、　それぞれ異なったものであり、「真正な公報」とは見なすことができないと考えます。

INPITのJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードして得られる「PDF公報」は、あくまでも「独自PDF公報」であって、「真正な公報」とは言えないものと考えます。

ましや、民間業者が作成する「独自PDF公報」も、これまた「真正な公報」と、言えません。

ここで、「独自PDF公報」の発行にあたって、INPITのJ-PlatPatにおいて奇怪な過去がありました。

何故か、２０２２年１月１２日〜１月２４日の１３日間のあいだ、J-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自ＰＤＦ公報」が異様なものでした。

https://t.co/iIBNCtOcDR

即ち、フロントページの右下に表示される「代表図面」、および３ページの図面が、一部欠けていました。

さらに、２０２２年１月２０日発行の「特開2022-014916」の独自PDF公報も代表図面と他の図面に欠落がありました。

https://t.co/fiIqp9T5N8

一方、民間業者である日立システムズのSRPARTNERよりダウンロードした「特開2022-014916」の独自PDF公報には欠落箇所はありませんでした。

https://t.co/lCT5dRre7A

J-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自ＰＤＦ公報」の異様さは同年１月の２４日まで続いたようです。

https://t.co/PrVwFrEG9m

代表図面（図３）の（２）の部分に、欠落がある。

このように１３日間も続いた、忌まわしい過去を持つINPITが提供するJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自ＰＤＦ公報」に、現時点において信頼性はあるのでしょうか、甚だ疑問に思います。

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

By combining [...] “Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise and AI into action,” said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company. “Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence.”

items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are | WIRED
items.summary: If AI is going to be one of the most significant advances in human civilization, then we should have an equally advanced political response. We should be making giant, no-regrets moves that give people and families economic resilience to withstand the changes. That is something that the richest nation on Earth at the richest moment in history, on the precipice of the greatest technological shift, can absolutely do. [...] I just think the issues presented by AI are so monstrously large, like: What is a person? What is writing? What is friendship? Would it be better to have artificial life forms than organic life forms? These are the monster questions that are typically the domain of the liberal arts, philosophy, and theology. There’s this strange new respect for it now. [...] Curiosity soon replaced my knee-jerk irritation. The summer of 2026 was a clear turning point in the AI narrative. Less than four years after ChatGPT launched, OpenAI software broke out of a supposedly safe test environment and hacked into a major open-source platform, Hugging Face. items.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
items.summary:
Within individual projects, AI capabilities were often requested alongside other work. AI-related postings listed about as many tasks as other postings but more often combined tasks that had rarely appeared together in earlier jobs.

### Example: Inside a project brief

Some clients asked for AI-generated video, editing, and motion graphics in a single posting. The freelancer would bring those skills together to deliver a finished video. [...] Show more

## Clients are asking for AI in more kinds of work and combining tasks in new ways

By late 2025, clients were requesting the use of AI in many more, different kinds of work. Clients were seeking freelancers to apply AI in tasks including chatbot development, video production, marketing automation, and application integration. [...] Because freelance projects turn over quickly, postings are continually refreshed as clients’ needs change. Work within firms can evolve without appearing in a new job posting. Combined with ChatGPT data, these postings offer an early view of which activities people undertake directly with AI, which they hire freelancers to perform, and how AI-related projects differ from other work.

items.title: Alphamin signs tin supply deal with Nathan Trotter - Mining Technology
items.summary: # Alphamin signs tin supply deal with Nathan Trotter. The agreement covers up to 3,600t of tin annually, about 20% of Bisie’s output, for two years. Alphamin Resources has entered an agreement to provide a portion of its tin concentrate production from the Bisie mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to Nathan Trotter in the US. The arrangement will allocate up to 3,600t of contained tin per year, or around 20% of Bisie’s annual production target, for an initial period of two years. Nathan Trotter is currently completing the construction of its smelting facility in the US. The new supply deal will help support this facility’s operations by securing a source of high-grade tin concentrate from Alphamin’s Bisie mine, which currently produces about 20,000t of contained tin annually. The company stated that supplying Nathan Trotter aligns with its strategy to support the development of tin refining capacity within western markets and to reduce concentration in global tin supply chains.

items.title: Op-Ed: Tin hit by AI stock rout despite physical market tightness - Mining.com
items.summary: Micro Gold Futures $ 4073 / ozt  -0.61%. Micro Silver Futures $ 51.955 / ozt  0.25%. Gold Futures $ 4073.2 / ozt  -0.62%. Tin, which had been riding the AI wave on the back of its use as an electronic solder, has taken a particularly hard knock after Wall Street lost $3.2 trillion in a single session on Thursday as investors feared Democrats could slow the buildout of AI data centers. London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month tin CMSN3 has slumped from over $50,000 per metric ton to an eight-month low of $45,360 in the space of a week. The bursting of tin’s AI-investment bubble is ironically ill-timed since the market is the tightest it’s been in many months. The benchmark cash-to-three-months spread CMSN0-3 was in a deep contango, with prompt tin at a discount of more than $350 per ton to three-month delivery in August. Off-warrant inventory has also fallen to 1,089 tons, down 1,535 tons since the start of the year.

items.title: Alphamin directs Congo tin to new US smelter - Mining.com
items.summary: Micro Gold Futures $ 4147.7 / ozt  1.79%. Gold Futures $ 4147.7 / ozt  1.80%. # Alphamin directs Congo tin to new US smelter. Henry Lazenby | November 9, 2026 | 2:28 pm  Base Metals News Africa United States Tin. Processing facilities at Alphamin Resources’ Bisie tin mine in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Alphamin Resources (TSXV: AFM; JSE: APH) has agreed to supply a new U.S. smelter with tin concentrate from the Democratic Republic of Congo, diversifying its sales as Washington backs domestic minerals processing. The material is destined for U.S. refiner Nathan Trotter & Co.’s $65-million (C$92 million) smelter in Virginia, which targets first production next year, Mauritius-based Alphamin said Monday. “Alphamin has been actively seeking to diversify its customer base and to support the development of western tin refining capacity,” the company said in a release. items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

items.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
items.summary:
Within individual projects, AI capabilities were often requested alongside other work. AI-related postings listed about as many tasks as other postings but more often combined tasks that had rarely appeared together in earlier jobs.

### Example: Inside a project brief

Some clients asked for AI-generated video, editing, and motion graphics in a single posting. The freelancer would bring those skills together to deliver a finished video. [...] Show more

## Clients are asking for AI in more kinds of work and combining tasks in new ways

By late 2025, clients were requesting the use of AI in many more, different kinds of work. Clients were seeking freelancers to apply AI in tasks including chatbot development, video production, marketing automation, and application integration. [...] Because freelance projects turn over quickly, postings are continually refreshed as clients’ needs change. Work within firms can evolve without appearing in a new job posting. Combined with ChatGPT data, these postings offer an early view of which activities people undertake directly with AI, which they hire freelancers to perform, and how AI-related projects differ from other work.

items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: You could manually program a robot to do a handful of tasks in a factory without issue—this type of automation has been common for decades. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google | TechCrunch
items.summary:
OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort, which had even included a “checkout cart” feature. [...] In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses. [...] Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products.

“As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.”

items.title: OpenAI gives brands free ChatGPT agents alongside paid ads
items.summary:
“The fact that OpenAI will now share insights itself will take some of the power away from the third-party companies,” she said. “But OpenAI isn’t going to share everything it knows, and ChatGPT is only one of several AI platforms, so demand for what the AI visibility companies offer will remain strong.”

Business Hub and agents are free for now but Shomair didn’t rule out a paid model in the future. [...] So, OpenAI has built two routes into the same conversation for brands, and only one of them costs money. One through ChatGPT’s organic recommendations, and the other via paid placements.

Shomair said early testing of sponsored agents had shown “promising results,” particularly in the depth of conversations between consumers and businesses.

“When a consumer chooses to engage more deeply with our business, there’s a high level of intent there,” he said. [...] OpenAI certainly thinks so. Businesses can now claim a profile in ChatGPT through a new Business Hub, get verified and feed in product and company details. In the U.S. (for now), e-commerce and online services businesses can go a step further and publish a business agent – a separately labelled chat that speaks for the brand once a user wants to dig into a product. OpenAI’s vp of monetization Benji Shomair declined to share a timeline for further rollout.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary: Google generated nearly $295 billion in advertising revenue last year. Search and other properties alone produced $225 billion—about $4.3 billion a week. The Trade Desk, the largest independent demand-side platform, booked $2.9 billion in annual revenue. Google’s search business generates more revenue in an average week than The Trade Desk does in a year. ChatGPT now sits at the same moment of expressed intent that Google has monetized so effectively. Whatever OpenAI calls its ad business, that [...] Of course, privacy is always a concern. People might be telling ChatGPT things they would never type into a search box, and no advertiser should get to read a conversation or see an individual prompt. Fine. Nobody is asking for that, and it isn’t an excuse. Google has worked around the same problem for decades. It limits, aggregates, and buckets the queries too rare to show, and advertisers still get what they need. The solutions are well known. OpenAI just doesn’t have the system—yet. [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.
